title: Warm-Start Quantum Computation: Spectral-Weight Resources for Energy Readout and State Preparation
summary: Estimating a ground-state energy and preparing a ground state both split into a front-end that supplies an approximate state $|χ\rangle$ and a back-end that reads or refines it. We argue, and measure at every step, that the only thing crossing that split is the front-end's spectral weight distribution $p_n=|\langle E_n|χ\rangle|^2$ over the eigenstates of the problem Hamiltonian $H_P$. Everything downstream is priced in it, so the front-end is a swappable module, and we swap it seven times without altering anything to its right. We call the arrangement WARP.
